settings.title: Water Alone Won't Carry You Through a Ten-Hour Shift.
settings.text: By the time you're thirsty you're already down. On a hot site you can sweat out one to two liters an hour, and chugging plain water dilutes the minerals you have left instead of replacing them. Losing just 2% of your body weight in sweat is enough to cut strength, coordination, and focus — the three things standing between you and a bad afternoon.

settings.title: Sodium Is What Makes the Water Stay.
settings.text: Sweat is salty for a reason. Every liter can carry up to 1,800mg of sodium out of you, and sodium is the mineral that pulls fluid into your bloodstream and holds it there. Drink water without it and most of it runs straight through. Tiiga uses 140mg of sodium citrate per stick — a gentle, all-day form that helps the water land without the seawater aftertaste of a salt-bomb packet.

settings.title: Potassium Works the Other Side of the Cell Wall.
settings.text: Sodium holds fluid around your cells. Potassium holds it inside them, and it's what fires every muscle contraction you make swinging a hammer or climbing scaffold. Run short and the first thing you notice is a calf that locks up on the drive home. Every Tiiga stick carries 352mg — more than a medium banana — from raw baobab fruit and organic coconut water, not a lab isolate.

settings.title: Magnesium: The One Nobody Bothers to Replace.
settings.text: Magnesium is a cofactor in more than 300 enzyme reactions, including the one that lets a contracted muscle let go again. Heavy physical work and heavy sweating both burn through it, and most guys on a jobsite never put any back. Tiiga adds 19mg of magnesium citrate — a daily topping-up dose meant to be taken every shift, not a one-time megadose that sends you looking for a porta-john.

settings.title: 73mg of Vitamin C. 80% of Your Day, Handled by 10 A.M.
settings.text: Sun, heat, diesel exhaust, welding fumes, silica dust, and hard physical output all push up oxidative stress — free radicals your body generates faster than it can clear them. Vitamin C is the water-soluble antioxidant that does the clearing, and your body doesn't store it, so yesterday's dose doesn't count today. Every Tiiga stick delivers 73mg, 80% of the Daily Value, most of it from raw baobab — one of the most vitamin-C-dense fruits on earth.

settings.question: Is 140mg of sodium enough if I sweat all day?
settings.answer: It depends on the day. Tiiga is dosed for all-day sipping, not for a single heavy-sweat replacement hit — that's why it doesn't taste salty. On a normal shift, one to two sticks alongside food covers most people. If you're working in extreme heat and losing multiple liters an hour, treat Tiiga as your daily base and add salt to your food or a high-sodium packet on the worst days.

settings.question: Why is there vitamin C in a hydration drink?
settings.answer: Because the jobsite generates oxidative stress — sun, heat, exhaust, welding fumes, dust, and hard physical output all produce free radicals faster than your body clears them. Vitamin C is the main water-soluble antioxidant that does that clearing, and your body doesn't store it. Every stick has 73mg, 80% of the Daily Value, most of it from raw baobab fruit rather than added synthetically.

settings.question: Will it crash me in the afternoon?
settings.answer: There's nothing in it to crash from. 35 calories, 0g added sugar, and no caffeine — sweetened with organic stevia extract. A sports drink puts 21g of sugar in you and takes it back out an hour later; this doesn't.

settings.question: Does it need a shaker bottle?
settings.answer: No. One 12g stick dissolves clear in a standard water bottle with a shake. No scoop, no clumps, no grit left at the bottom of the jug.

settings.question: Can I drink it every single day?
settings.answer: That's how it's built. The doses are daily-use amounts rather than megadoses — including the magnesium, which is why it won't send you looking for a porta-john. Plenty of customers run one stick every morning and a second one on hot days.

settings.question: What does the prebiotic fiber have to do with hydration?
settings.answer: Two things. Soluble fiber slows how fast fluid and sugar move through you, which helps you hold onto what you drink. And 5g of raw baobab fiber a day feeds the gut bacteria that gas-station and break-room food starves. It's the part of the formula no electrolyte packet has.

settings.question: How is this different from the electrolyte packet at the gas station?
settings.answer: Most packets are mineral salts and flavoring. Tiiga is more than 75% whole food — raw baobab fruit and organic coconut water — which is where the potassium, the fiber, and most of the vitamin C come from. You're getting a wider spread of what the job takes out of you, not just a sodium hit.
